queries.text: How did American cities change across four decades (1980-2024): gentrification, inequality, affordability, and displacement — every claim cited?
Median home price in major US metros 1980 vs 2024
Share of households earning less than 30% Area Median Income (AMI) in US cities 1980-2024
Gini coefficient for income inequality in top 50 US metropolitan statistical areas by decade from 1980 to 2020
Percentage change in rent-to-income ratio for renters in New York City, Los Angeles, and Chicago between 1980 and 2023
Number of neighborhoods classified as gentrified according to the American Community Survey definition per metro area from 2000 to 2022
Median household income growth rate versus median home price appreciation rate in San Francisco from 1990 to 2023
Share of low-income households displaced due to housing costs in Washington DC, Boston, and Seattle between 2015 and 2024
Count of affordable rental units lost or converted to market-rate in Austin, Denver, and Phoenix from 2010 to 2024
Percentage point change in racial segregation index for Black residents in major US cities between 1980 census data and 2020 Census data
Ratio of median renter burden (housing cost as percentage of income) exceeding 50% by city tier (large metro vs small town) across decades 1980s through 2020s

search_hits.title: Urban Gentrification Metrics: Four Decades of American City Transformation (the exemplar report)
search_hits.snippet: The operator's exemplar report (vendored as source-report.pdf): New York City leads with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469 versus the national average of 0.40 in 2013, while Atlanta and Miami follow at 0.57 and New Orleans at 0.56; the Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 (+225% since January 2000); 48 of the 50 largest metros saw worsening mobility with Houston the sole improvement (+1.1%).
